findings.title: Unnecessarily technical product language
findings.evidence: Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.
findings.why: I have to work out what the service actually does, and the jargon makes it feel less warm and trustworthy for a family keepsake.

findings.title: Testimonials provide few trust details
findings.evidence: “My daughter asks for ‘her’ book every single night.” — Hannah, Leeds
findings.why: The quote sounds nice, but I cannot tell whether it comes from a real verified customer or gives any useful information about the finished product.

findings.title: Email and password fields have no persistent labels
findings.evidence: [5] and [6] are listed as “textbox (no label)” and rely only on the placeholders “Email” and “Password”.
findings.why: The placeholders make the form understandable visually, but persistent labels would make it clearer which field is which and more accessible.

findings.title: Unexplained technical sync error
findings.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
findings.why: I cannot tell whether my family details are missing, whether creating a book will work, or what I should do about it.

findings.title: Error gives no recovery action
findings.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.” with no visible retry or help control
findings.why: I am left wondering whether the page is genuinely broken and what to do next.

findings.title: Generic account greeting
findings.evidence: “Welcome back, Demo”
findings.why: It is functional, but using the actual account name would feel more reassuring and personal.

findings.title: Singular character field contradicts plural wording
findings.evidence: The heading says “Who else is in the story?” but there is only [10] “Who else is in the story?” textbox.
findings.why: I may think I have missed controls for adding several people, or assume Grandpa Joe's name needs to be written in an unusual combined format.

findings.title: Optional appearance field may be too restrictive for the planned memory
findings.evidence: [9] “What do they look like? (optional)” has placeholder “e.g. curly red hair, green welllies” and there is no field for Grandpa Joe's grey hair.
findings.why: Sam can be described, but the second person may not be visually represented accurately unless there is another step or free-text detail field.

findings.title: Footer text has very low contrast
findings.evidence: The footer links and copyright text, including “Privacy”, “Terms”, and “Contact”, appear extremely faint against the background.
findings.why: I can barely read the privacy, terms, and contact information.

findings.title: Reading level is labelled with Lexile rather than a child’s age
findings.evidence: “Lexile BR–200L,” “Lexile 200L–500L,” “Lexile 500L–800L,” and “Lexile 800L+”
findings.why: I am choosing a book for a five-year-old, but I do not know which Lexile range is right for her.

findings.title: File upload has no programmatic label
findings.evidence: [30] file-upload (no label) shows only the browser text “Choose file” and “No file chosen”.
findings.why: I can see what the control does from the surrounding instructions, but its purpose is not clearly named in the interface itself.

findings.title: Footer text has very low contrast
findings.evidence: The footer links “Privacy”, “Terms”, and “Contact” and the copyright line are extremely pale against the background.
findings.why: I can barely notice or read the privacy and contact information, which matters when uploading a child’s photo.

findings.title: Loading state has no explanation
findings.evidence: The central panel contains only a loading spinner and no status text.
findings.why: I cannot tell whether my book is actually being created or whether something has gone wrong.

findings.title: Typo in generated title
findings.evidence: “The Magical Adventrue of Sam”
findings.why: It makes the finished book look careless and undermines my confidence in the rest of the story.

findings.title: Selected illustration style appears not to have been applied
findings.evidence: The page says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic,” although the story setup said “soft watercolour illustrations.”
findings.why: I chose the visual style specifically, so this looks like the website ignored an important choice.

findings.title: Cover illustration may not reflect the supplied character details
findings.evidence: The cover shows a generic child labelled “Sam,” with no visible brown hair or connection to Grandpa Joe or the beach memory.
findings.why: I expected a personalised family memory book, so a cover that does not visibly use the supplied details is disappointing.

findings.title: Ordering control is below the fold
findings.evidence: [9] link “Order hardcover” is marked offscreen.
findings.why: I can see that ordering exists, but I cannot immediately tell whether it is available without scrolling through the preview.

findings.title: Hardcover price is not shown before ordering
findings.evidence: [9] link "Order hardcover" and [8] button "Regenerate entire book – $4.99"; no hardcover price is visible beside the order link.
findings.why: I want to know what a printed hardcover costs before I commit to entering the checkout.

findings.title: Paid regeneration control is prominent beside ordering
findings.evidence: [8] button "Regenerate entire book – $4.99" appears immediately beside the orange “Order hardcover” link.
findings.why: I am here to order the book, and the paid regeneration button could be easy to press by accident while looking for the order controls.

findings.title: Premium gift wrap is pre-selected without being requested
findings.evidence: [6] checkbox “Premium gift wrap” (checked) and “£7.99”
findings.why: It makes the real cost higher without my consent and makes me distrust the checkout.

findings.title: The final cost may be difficult to understand at a glance
findings.evidence: “Hardcover: The Magical Adventrue of Sam £24.99”, “Premium gift wrap £7.99”, “Shipping & handling £12.99”, and “Total £45.97”
findings.why: I can see the arithmetic, but £12.99 shipping is expensive and the page does not explain what delivery level or timeframe it provides.

findings.title: The generated title contains a spelling error
findings.evidence: “Hardcover: The Magical Adventrue of Sam”
findings.why: I would be embarrassed to receive a personalised book with such an obvious mistake in the title.

findings.title: Countdown-style price reservation may create unnecessary urgency
findings.evidence: "Your price is reserved for 09:40"
findings.why: It pressures me to decide quickly even though the checkout has no clear explanation of what happens when the timer expires.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: The title reads “The Magical Adventrue of Sam.”

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The cover shows a generic figure, star, and sun but omits the beach, sandcastles, yellow bucket, brown-haired five-year-old girl, and Grandpa Joe.

findings.title: visual_quality
findings.evidence: The picture is a sparse geometric graphic labelled “Pop-art comic,” not the requested soft watercolour style, and the generated “Sam” label overlaps the ground.

findings.title: character_consistency
findings.evidence: Sam is presented as an androgynous figure in a green top with short brown hair, with no clear visual indication that she is a five-year-old girl.

findings.title: emotional_resonance
findings.evidence: Nothing in the image represents the specific memory of building sandcastles with Grandpa Joe.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The supplied memory was “A day at the beach building sandcastles with Grandpa Joe,” but Grandpa Joe and the sandcastle-building event are absent.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: “Once upon a time, in the beach” uses the wrong construction; this should be “at the beach.”

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The text says Sam loves a yellow bucket, while the picture contains a yellow star and no bucket.

findings.title: character_consistency
findings.evidence: The simple figure has short brown hair, but nothing in the drawing clearly establishes Sam as a five-year-old girl.

findings.title: emotional_resonance
findings.evidence: The opening uses stock fantasy phrasing and does not introduce the warm grandfather-child relationship that made the memory special.

findings.title: age_fit
findings.evidence: “The ephemeral luminescence of the crepuscular firmament engendered an inexplicable melancholy” contains vocabulary far beyond a five-year-old's reading level.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: Although grammatically elaborate, the sentence is wildly unsuitable for the requested age; the automatic measurement also gives the prose a grade 7.0 level.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: The sudden shift to evening and abstract melancholy is not connected to the requested beach memory or any action involving Grandpa Joe.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: This invented melancholy scene has no basis in the supplied memory and displaces the sandcastle activity.

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The picture captures evening and stars, but it cannot convey the advanced emotions or elaborate wording in the text.

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The text describes pouring rain, grey drops, puddles, and a hood, while the picture shows a bright sun and clear blue sky.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: The child's name is incorrectly rendered as “Samn.”

findings.title: character_consistency
findings.evidence: Samn is not the supplied name, and the image still shows the original figure without a hood or rain protection.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The yellow star in the image does not match the yellow bucket described in the text.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: The sudden storm is introduced without setup and does not lead into the requested sandcastle memory with Grandpa Joe.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The user specified “Grandpa Joe” with the relationship “Grandparent,” but the output invents “Uncle Bartholomew” and omits Grandpa Joe.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: “He called, and he followed him” makes the pronouns and direction of action ambiguous.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: A lantern-bearing uncle suddenly appears, but there is no setup for why he is there or how the story moved from the beach to “the winding path.”

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The image shows the two figures and a possible lantern, but no visible winding path and no transition from the beach.

findings.title: character_consistency
findings.evidence: Sam is drawn with the same short brown hair, but the invented uncle is given a full appearance and label that was never requested.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The supplied event was building sandcastles with Grandpa Joe at the beach; the story instead invents a lost-child sequence in the woods with a red balloon.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: The story jumps from Grandpa Joe's beach outing to Sam being alone in deep woods without explaining how she got there.

findings.title: age_fit
findings.evidence: “The shadows grew teeth and whispered that no one would ever find Sam again” is frightening and emotionally unsuitable for the requested gentle age-five beach story.

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The text describes shadows with teeth and whispering danger, but the picture shows harmless round trees and a calm moonlit scene.

findings.title: character_consistency
findings.evidence: Sam's shirt changes from green in earlier pages to teal here, and the picture does not show Grandpa Joe beside her.

findings.title: emotional_resonance
findings.evidence: The threatening separation is not based on my memory and makes the keepsake feel upsetting rather than affectionate.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The memory called for Sam and Grandpa Joe to build sandcastles together, but the conclusion says only that “Sam skipped all the way home.”

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: “Once upon a time, in the beach, there lived a curious child named Sam” repeats the opening almost exactly after the intervening events.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: “Once upon a time, in the beach” is an incorrect and awkward construction.

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The text describes skipping all the way home, but the picture shows Sam standing still with no home, path, or movement.

findings.title: character_consistency
findings.evidence: Sam's basic design remains similar, but she is again alone and Grandpa Joe is absent.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: “And from that day on, whenever Sam looked up at the sky, she would always remember” ends without saying what she remembered.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: “The End” is printed twice in the text.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The final memory never explicitly recalls building sandcastles with Grandpa Joe, and the yellow bucket is absent.

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The picture only shows Sam and “The End”; it does not depict the sky, the completed memory, Grandpa Joe, the sandcastle, or the bucket.

findings.title: emotional_resonance
findings.evidence: The unfinished sentence and plain final illustration prevent the book from feeling like a meaningful family keepsake.

findings.title: visual_quality
findings.evidence: The large empty orange field and generic repeated figure make the concluding page visually plain.
